claims.claim: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited is the issuer underlying NYSE ADR ticker TSM; current company financial evidence is sourced from TSMC investor-relations primary materials and market observations are kept as a separate origin.

Q2 2026 operating figures are current primary issuer evidence published July 16, 2026; issuer earnings release, quarterly-results page and transcript are duplicate issuer-origin families for independence purposes and are not counted as independent corroboration.
September 17, 2026 ADR price/valuation observations are external market-data evidence and remain distinct from issuer-origin operating evidence.

risks.risk: Issuer-origin materials dominate operating and technology evidence; external market data independently addresses valuation but not competitive claims.

unknowns.unknown: No independent source is used to upgrade management forecasts for Q3 2026 or long-run node leadership; forecasts remain issuer guidance until realized.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue was NT$1,270.38B, up 36.0% year over year and 12.0% sequentially; net income was NT$706.56B, up 77.4% year over year.
Q2 gross margin was 67.7%, operating margin 60.3%, and advanced technologies at 7nm and below represented 77% of wafer revenue; 2nm contributed 3% during its early ramp.

TSMC ended Q2 with approximately NT$3.5T of cash and marketable securities and generated about NT$783B operating cash flow while spending NT$496B in capex, supporting substantial self-funded expansion capacity.

Management guided Q3 2026 revenue to US$44.6B-US$45.8B with 65%-67% gross margin and 56%-58% operating margin, explicitly citing continued leading-edge demand and steep 2nm ramp; this is a future execution checkpoint, not realized evidence.
TSM ADR closed September 17, 2026 at $430.26; external market data showed roughly $2.0T market capitalization, trailing P/E about 28.3x and forward P/E about 19.5x.

TSMC's board has ten members and includes multiple independent directors; Chairman C.C. Wei also serves as CEO, creating strong operating authority but less chair/CEO separation than a fully independent-chair structure.

thesisQuality.basis: Realized leading-edge growth, extraordinary margins, massive self-funded capex capacity and centrality to advanced semiconductor manufacturing support an exceptional thesis; geopolitical and concentration risks prevent a maximum.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 revenue rose 36.0% YoY and 12.0% sequentially while net income rose 77.4% YoY; gross and operating margins reached 67.7% and 60.3%.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At $430.26 and roughly $2.0T market capitalization, trailing P/E near 28.3x and forward P/E near 19.5x are not distressed but remain moderate relative to current growth and profitability; geopolitical tail risk warrants conservatism.

catalystScore.basis: Q3 guidance calls for $44.6B-$45.8B revenue and a steep 2nm ramp after 2nm already reached 3% of Q2 wafer revenue, creating a near-term measurable catalyst.

governancePower.basis: A ten-member globally experienced board with multiple independent directors provides oversight, while combined Chairman/CEO authority at C.C. Wei reduces structural separation and caps the assessment.

alignment2036.basis: TSMC is foundational manufacturing infrastructure for advanced compute, AI, communications and heterogeneous semiconductor systems; 77% of Q2 wafer revenue came from 7nm-and-below technologies.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Leading-edge process manufacturing serves multiple compute, communications and semiconductor end markets and compounds ecosystem leverage across successive nodes.

bottleneckControl.basis: The steep 2nm ramp and 77% advanced-node mix evidence direct control over scarce leading-edge fabrication capacity that constrains advanced computing supply.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Broad end-market exposure, exceptional profitability and large liquidity support resilience across demand scenarios; geographic/geopolitical concentration materially limits robustness.

substitutionResilience.basis: Successive leading-edge node ramps, advanced-node revenue dominance and extreme capital intensity create high substitution barriers, though Samsung/Intel foundry and customer vertical integration remain credible alternatives.

supplyChainResilience.basis: NT$3.5T cash and marketable securities plus very strong operating cash flow support redundancy and capacity investment, but Taiwan-centered leading-edge manufacturing and equipment/material dependencies remain material concentration risks.

pricingPower.basis: Q2 gross margin of 67.7% and operating margin of 60.3% alongside 36% YoY revenue growth demonstrate exceptional economics and pricing/mix power at leading-edge nodes.

riskEvidence.basis: Exceptional liquidity, margins and node leadership offset major Taiwan geopolitical/geographic concentration, cyclicality, enormous capital intensity, customer concentration and alternative-foundry risks.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current primary quarterly operating evidence and governance material cover the required operating/governance factors, with current independent market data for valuation; detailed customer/supplier concentration and geopolitical scenario probabilities remain explicit non-gating unknowns.

riskEvidence.basis: Leadership/liquidity offset geopolitical, geographic, cyclicality, capex and concentration risk.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current issuer operating/governance evidence plus current external valuation evidence; residual concentration/geopolitical unknowns preserved.

scoreRecord.thesis: TSMC combines exceptional realized financial momentum with dominant control of leading-edge fabrication bottlenecks and a steep 2nm ramp, making it foundational to 2036 compute infrastructure; geopolitical concentration is the principal structural counterweight.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A Taiwan geopolitical disruption, geographic manufacturing concentration, customer/platform concentration or successful foundry substitution could impair a business whose valuation now reflects substantial continued leadership.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 results and 2nm ramp evidence against management's $44.6B-$45.8B revenue and 65%-67% gross-margin guidance.

risks.risk: Taiwan geopolitical/geographic concentration is the dominant tail risk despite global expansion and liquidity.
Leading-edge capex intensity and customer concentration can amplify cyclical or platform-specific shocks.

unknowns.unknown: Exact current top-customer and critical-equipment supplier concentration are not quantified in this evidence object.
Q3 guidance and steep 2nm ramp remain forward-looking until filed/realized.
